A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and references support comparison after accounting for substantial reformatting. Neither PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports findings attributed to surveyed research, alongside conceptual taxonomies and mathematical background. It does not report original experiments or empirical data analysis.

after.justification: Section 6.4 adds an author-attributed descriptive analysis of reviewed studies: approximately two-thirds emphasize pass@1 improvements and one-third report expanded pass@k frontiers. This constitutes an original cross-study result, although its counting procedure is undocumented. The new benchmark plots compile results from surveyed methods.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an implemented learning algorithm or model. Expanded descriptions of existing algorithms, code world models, and deployment architectures change the survey's exposition and coverage rather than a proposed method.

E1.justification: No new training or benchmark execution by the survey authors is reported. CWMB and Code Simulation are newly discussed resources; the new score compilations and cross-study analysis concern the already covered coding and mathematical-reasoning domains.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Figures 7–8 compile scores for previously discussed methods, while newly surveyed approaches do not become experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Table 5 revises reported model configurations for surveyed studies. Satori-SWE changes from Qwen-2.5-Math-7B to Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct, and Posterior-GRPO's 7B entry changes from Base to Instruct. These are revisions to reported settings, without evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 6.4 adds a limited cross-study analysis of whether RL primarily improves sampling accuracy or expands reasoning capabilities, supported by approximate counts of pass@1-focused and pass@k-frontier studies. The added Deep Research and Voyager descriptions are principally explanatory case discussions.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added. The new plots and approximate study proportions supply point summaries without statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 7–8 substantially expand numerical reporting with coding and mathematics benchmark-score compilations; Section 6.4 adds the approximate two-thirds versus one-third study proportions. Existing rStar2-Agent AIME24/AIME25 scores remain 80.6%/69.8%. The new plots combine heterogeneous models and pass@k budgets, so they do not establish comparable-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The MDP/POMDP formulations and Equations 1–17 retain their mathematical substance. Tuple ordering, notation, and expanded explanations of standard RL algorithms do not introduce new definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: distinguishing Agentic RL through an MDP/POMDP perspective, organizing capabilities and applications into two taxonomies, and consolidating research resources.

C2.justification: V4 substantially expands interpretation through the mathematical-reasoning case study, distinctions among multi-agent optimization regimes, and discussion of credit assignment and scalability. New Sections 6.5–6.6 address deployment architectures, human oversight, misuse, sustainability, labor effects, bias, and evaluation contamination.

D1.justification: Table 5 fills missing model information for PSGPO and Qwen3-Coder and changes Satori-SWE's resource link. Section 4.2.4 adds quantization and hardware guidance. Conversely, v4 removes the direct companion-repository link and Table 2's explicit clipping, KL-penalty, and training-signal columns.

R1.justification: The literature synthesis expands substantially into code world models, including GIF-MCTS, WorldCoder, and CWM, and into deployment protocols and societal impacts. Additional foundational citations strengthen the discussion of policy gradients and dual-process reasoning. These changes extend research positioning beyond bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: V4 includes widespread copyediting, expanded algorithm explanations, and reorganizes Section 4.7 into three optimization regimes. It removes the contents pages and acknowledgments and introduces additional subsections, while retaining the overall seven-section narrative and much of the existing prose.

P2.justification: The journal format changes typography, headers, and placement throughout. V4 adds benchmark plots in Figures 7–8 and the application-capability matrix in Table 9, expands v2's Figure 4 into Figure 5 with explanatory side panels, and substantially restructures Table 2.

improvement.justification: Table 9 connects the two taxonomies more clearly, the reorganized multi-agent section provides useful distinctions, and Sections 6.5–6.6 strengthen practical interpretation and limitations. Technical-entry revisions also improve the reference material. These gains are moderated by undocumented study proportions, heterogeneous benchmark compilations, and removal of the direct companion-repository link and contents pages.
